entities.name: PMID:25085524
observations: 2014 BMC Cancer study: ΔNp63α directly regulated GLI2 in osteosarcoma cells; SaOS-2-ΔNp63α cells showed tumorigenic attributes in vitro, and the authors reported ΔNp63α–GLI2 crosstalk as necessary for progression. Abstract lists wound-healing, colony-formation, and proliferation assays.

entities.name: ΔNp63α
observations: In osteosarcoma cell assays, reported to directly regulate GLI2 transcription and contribute to tumorigenic attributes.

entities.name: GLI2
observations: Reported as a direct transcriptional target of ΔNp63α in osteosarcoma cells; ΔNp63α–GLI2 crosstalk was described as necessary for progression.

entities.name: Osteosarcoma progression
observations: In vitro osteosarcoma study associated ΔNp63α–GLI2 crosstalk with tumorigenic phenotypes assessed using migration/wound-healing, colony-formation, and proliferation assays.
